rationale: This is a tiny (3 functions, ~1 KB text) floating-point-heavy numeric benchmark with a hot 4x4 matmul kernel, so the priority is arithmetic-level obfuscation with minimal loop-body overhead: SUB gets the highest SecurityGain/DiversityGain because instruction substitution directly obscures the arithmetic and its FP-heavy features favor it, with only moderate RuntimeCost tolerance since substituted sequences execute on every inner-loop iteration and CorrectnessRisk kept low because substitution on double-precision code must stay conservative. BCF and FLA are de-prioritized (low RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights) because bogus control flow and dispatcher-based flattening inflate both size and per-iteration branch cost in tight kernels, and this program's control flow is trivial (small loops, little to hide); FLA keeps a modest security weight since flattening wrap_mul4's structure still aids resistance at acceptable risk. SPLIT is cheap and safe (high cost tolerance, lowest correctness risk) so it is enabled as a low-overhead diversity contributor. IBR gets moderate weights as a middle-ground control-flow hardener. ICALL and IGV are largely neutralized by the program's profile — almost no indirect-call sites and essentially no global-variable state in a 3-function binary — so they receive the lowest security/diversity weights and are effectively disabled in practice, avoiding their correctness and runtime exposure where they have nothing to hide.
